clue.text: Student making love with undies regularly spread

parts.note: L is the learner driver's plate, so a student
slang: a couple 'at it' are making love

indicators.note: regularly asks for every other letter of the word undies, starting with the first

explanation.surface: A student's romantic encounter, with underwear scattered about the room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' looks like part of the bedroom picture, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Latitude is scope or room to range freely, a breadth or extent, which is a spread.

clue.text: Dives in ice after slipping on the fence

indicators.note: the words dives in ice have slipped, their letters sliding into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone dives into an icy pool after losing their footing on a fence.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sitting on the fence will not commit to either side, so they are undecided.

clue.text: Rearrange spa visit

definitions.meaning: to ... is to sort again, putting into a new order
a spa town is a health ...
to ... to a place is to go there often, to frequent or visit it

explanation.surface: An instruction to reschedule a trip to a health spa.
explanation.definitionFit: Three senses of one spelling: sort again, a holiday destination, and to frequent a place.

clue.text: E-cigarette's case stays in need of repair

indicators.note: something broken and in need of repair is in disorder, so these letters get rearranged
the case of a word is its outer shell, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: The casing of an e-cigarette keeps breaking and needs fixing.
explanation.walkthrough: The E of 'E-cigarette' stands alone as the definition: E is slang for the drug. The case of cigarette gives CE, shuffled with STAYS.
explanation.definitionFit: E is the common street abbreviation for the drug ecstasy, MDMA.

clue.text: Contract muscle to fix a four-horse chariot

parts.note: the quadriceps muscle, contracted or shortened, is the quad
to rig something is to fix it dishonestly, as with a rigged race

explanation.surface: A charioteer flexes a muscle to secure a four-horse chariot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contract' reads as a verb for flexing the muscle, but it says the muscle's name is shortened.
explanation.definitionFit: A quadriga is the Roman chariot drawn by four horses abreast.

clue.text: Read out sensible explanations

indicators.note: read out means spoken, so the word is heard rather than seen

parts.note: a sensible person is wise

explanation.surface: Someone reads sensible explanations aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: The whys of something are its reasons, the explanations for why it is so.

clue.text: Tax-free scheme's ending to replace agreement

parts.note: something tax-free carries no VAT, value added tax

indicators.note: the ending of the word scheme's is its last letter

explanation.surface: A tax-free savings scheme closes and a new agreement takes its place.
explanation.walkthrough: VAT is value added tax, the British sales tax.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, to novate is to substitute a new contract for an existing one, replacing the agreement.

clue.text: Schwarzenegger chasing the lead in major Hitchcock film

indicators.note: chasing means coming after, so this piece follows the other
the lead in a word is its opening letter

parts.note: Arnold Schwarzenegger is popularly called Arnie

explanation.surface: Schwarzenegger pursuing the lead role in a major Hitchcock picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Marnie is Alfred Hitchcock's 1964 thriller starring Tippi Hedren and Sean Connery.

clue.text: Took off coat and hung out

indicators.note: out here means put out of place, so the letters of coat and hung are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone removed their coat and then spent time relaxing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hung out' reads as relaxing, but 'out' is the anagram signal on COAT and HUNG; 'and' just joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: A trend that took off became popular quickly, which is what caught on means.

clue.text: Rescue craft, if able to anyway

indicators.note: anyway means in any way at all, so the letters can go in any order

explanation.surface: A rescue boat that should launch if it can, whatever happens.
explanation.definitionFit: A lifeboat is a vessel launched to save people in danger at sea.

clue.text: Shake up trash can

parts.note: to dis is slang for to trash or disparage
may and can both express permission

explanation.surface: An instruction to rattle a rubbish bin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trash can' reads as one American noun, but it splits into two verbs.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismay someone is to upset or unsettle them, to shake them up.

clue.text: Project entertaining porky playgirl?

indicators.note: entertaining means holding as a guest, so one piece holds the other inside

parts.note: to jut is to project or stick out
porky is short for pork pie, rhyming slang for a lie

explanation.surface: A scheme that involves a plump playgirl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'porky' is British rhyming slang: pork pie means lie.
explanation.definitionFit: Juliet is the heroine of Shakespeare's Romeo and Juliet, so a girl in a play; the question mark flags the pun.

clue.text: It helps you to generate capital

definitions.text: It helps you to generate capital

parts.words: It helps you to generate capital
parts.note: the capital here is a capital letter, which a keyboard key produces when held

explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' suggests money and investment, but it means an upper-case letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Holding this keyboard key down makes the letter keys type upper case.

clue.text: Beginning parts of 23A, 10A, 8A, 20A, 11A, 18D, 12A, 9A, 26A, 22D, 7D, 2D and 21D

parts.note: these twelve answers each hold a month's abbreviation, JAN to DEC in order, and the months are the parts of the year
the answer to 21 down, period, means a full stop or dot

explanation.surface: An index pointing to the opening letters of thirteen other answers.
explanation.walkthrough: TROJAN, LIFEBOAT, MARNIE, APRES-SKI, DISMAY, JUNCTION, JULIET, CAUGHT ON, HOSEPIPE, OCTAVE, NOVATE and INDECISIVE hold JAN to DEC; 'Beginning' is the definition, not an instruction to take first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: From the year dot is an idiom meaning from the very start of time, the earliest beginning.

clue.text: Some feel big election setback is understandable

indicators.note: a setback sets the letters back, so they are read in the opposite direction
some of these words means only part of their letters, a run inside them

explanation.surface: Some people feel that a big electoral defeat is easy to understand.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing that is legible can be read clearly, so it is understandable.

clue.text: After this, Verity is very close to snapping

parts.note: if the name Verity loses the letters I and T, what remains is the word very

explanation.surface: A woman named Verity is on the verge of a breakdown after some event.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer read as an instruction: VERITY losing IT leaves VERY. 'this' stands for the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Losing it is an idiom for losing control of one's temper or composure, being about to snap.

clue.text: Breeder's top setter bites jeans — naughty dog!

indicators.note: the setter clamps on at the end, biting onto the jeans letters as the last piece
the top of a word is its first letter
naughty means misbehaving, so the letters will not stay in their places

parts.note: the setter of a crossword refers to themself as I

explanation.surface: A breeder's prize setter chews through some jeans, the bad dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' sounds like a dog breed, but it is the crossword setter, I.
explanation.definitionFit: The basenji is a barkless hunting dog breed from central Africa.

clue.text: Raj's bottom cream is a turn-off

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom of a word is its final letter

parts.note: unction is an ointment or cream used for anointing

explanation.surface: Raj's bottom cream is unappealing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn-off' looks like something off-putting but is literal: a place to turn off a road.
explanation.definitionFit: A road junction is where one road branches from another, a place to turn off.

clue.text: Hell-bent agent commandeers cab travelling north

indicators.note: to commandeer a cab is to take it over, holding it within

parts.note: a fed is a US federal agent

indicators.note: in a down clue going north reads the word from bottom to top

parts.note: a cab is a taxi

explanation.surface: A determined agent seizes a taxi heading north.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone fixated is obsessed with one aim, as single-minded as someone hell-bent on it.

clue.text: Half kiss a crush before evening of fun

indicators.note: the earlier pieces come before the kiss piece in the answer

parts.note: to crush is to press

indicators.note: half of the word kiss is its first two letters

explanation.surface: A quick peck and a hug ahead of a fun night out.
explanation.definitionFit: Après-ski is the socialising in bars and resorts after a day on the slopes, often an evening's entertainment.

clue.text: Stretch and point across the pond

definitions.meaning: Across the pond means in the US

explanation.surface: Stretch out and point toward the far side of a pond.
explanation.definitionFit: Period means a span of time, and is the American word for the punctuation mark ending a sentence.

clue.text: Masses from the Deep South

parts.note: the deep is a poetic name for the ocean
S is the compass abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: Religious services held in the American Deep South.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Masses' reads as church services, but it means large amounts.
explanation.definitionFit: Oceans of something means great quantities of it, masses or loads.

clue.text: One covered in scales swimming at cove

indicators.note: swimming letters are moving about, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A scaly fish swimming in a coastal cove.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scales' suggests a fish, but it means musical scales.
explanation.definitionFit: An octave is the span of eight notes, which a musical scale covers from one note to its repeat.

clue.text: Surprisingly, disheartened janitor is hard worker

indicators.note: surprisingly signals the remaining letters come out in an unexpected order
losing its heart, the word janitor drops its central letter

explanation.surface: A downhearted caretaker turns out to be a diligent employee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' takes I, the middle of JANITOR, leaving JANTOR to be shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: To work like a Trojan is an idiom for working very hard, so a Trojan is a tireless worker.

clue.text: My Zoom employee evaluation: "Jolly at first, then all upset"

indicators.note: in a down clue all upset means the whole run is turned upside down, read bottom to top
at first asks for the opening letter of each of these words

explanation.surface: An online performance review that started jovially and ended in distress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' looks like a possessive but is the exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: My! and Jeez! are both mild exclamations of surprise or exasperation.

clue.text: State of otherness that's found close to 13, become weary about unknown

parts.note: 13 across is the shift key, and the Alt key sits next to it on a keyboard

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to tire is to become weary
Y is one of the letters used for an unknown in algebra

explanation.surface: A philosophical state found near a key, tied to fatigue and mystery.
explanation.definitionFit: Alterity is a philosophical term for being other or different, otherness itself.

clue.text: Bed wetter pees uncontrollably over character behind house

indicators.note: behind means this piece comes after the house piece
over means placed across, so these letters straddle the character
done uncontrollably, the letters fall in no fixed order

parts.note: pi is a Greek character or letter

explanation.surface: A child who wets the bed and cannot control it, near the back of a house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bed wetter' suggests a child, but the bed is a flower bed and a hosepipe waters it; 'over' means the shuffled letters sit on both sides of the Greek character.
explanation.definitionFit: A hosepipe is used in the garden to water flower beds.

clue.text: The clap shared between two old couples is a magical thing

indicators.note: the two letters are split up, one going with each couple of letters

parts.note: the clap is slang for gonorrhoea, a VD or venereal disease
a couple of old gives two O's, O being the abbreviation for old
the second couple of O's, each O standing for old

explanation.surface: A sexually transmitted disease passed among two elderly couples is a kind of magic.
explanation.walkthrough: V takes the first OO and D the second, giving VOO + DOO.
explanation.definitionFit: Voodoo is a religion and system of magic from Haiti, and loosely any magic spell or charm.
